title: Choose RallyLoop’s visual world
question: The roll assigned Labanotation. Keep it, choose an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Movement Score
options.thesis: A live session read as movement, position, and time.
options.viewport: A clear session workspace leads with who is waiting, which courts are active, and the next staff action. A restrained mirrored court/time mark carries the notation system.
options.risk: The notation is unfamiliar outside dance; keep court and queue labels literal.

raised.raise: A changed court stays attached to its row and remains marked until staff have seen the update.
Keyboard focus reveals one session’s secondary details in place; it never becomes a poster rail.
Court diagrams keep a consistent scale so occupancy is comparable across the product.
Reduced-motion mode settles live state changes directly, without interpolating queue positions.

options.label: Club Match Sheet
options.lineage: Printed club fixtures and court-side score sheets
options.thesis: The club’s match sheet, made live and easy to scan.
options.viewport: A standard app shell names the facility and session. The queue and live courts lead, with a clear next-player action and a match-sheet rhythm in the typography and status marks.
options.risk: Familiar and effective; avoid making every screen look like a literal printed sheet.

options.label: Gate Board
options.lineage: Boarding passes and live departure boards
options.thesis: The queue is a live ranking whose changes stay visible.
options.viewport: A familiar facility/session shell leads to live court rows and a time-ordered player queue; a court change moves with its row and remains briefly highlighted.
options.case: Strong operational clarity for changing queues; travel imagery is less native to a sports club.
options.risk: Can feel like an airport reskin if the product’s court and player language is not dominant.

options.label: Court Wayfinding
options.thesis: Every screen makes the next court decision obvious.
options.viewport: The familiar app shell stays intact; clear sign-like court labels and a strong next-step cue help players locate their court and staff move a queue forward.
options.case: Excellent directional clarity; the venue-sign system is less specific to recreational sports than the picked club sheet.
options.risk: Yellow must remain purposeful wayfinding, not fill the whole interface.

options.label: Streaming Catalog
options.thesis: A wall of sessions opens detail as each one is focused.
options.case: Sessions can be browsed as objects, but a media-wall pattern weakens the live queue task.
options.kept: Focused sessions can reveal useful secondary details without a route change.
options.risk: The poster-wall structure is too browsing-led for live facility operations.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: A measured sequence keeps each court and match in proportion.
options.case: Precise comparisons help, but botanical language does not identify the sports-club audience.
options.kept: Comparable court views should preserve one consistent scale.
options.risk: The folio’s archival character is too far from a live session.

options.label: Variable Specimen
options.thesis: One live state changes every part of the display in step.
options.case: Responsive type is expressive, but font axes add little to queue and court operations.
options.kept: Respect reduced motion and provide settled states for live changes.
options.risk: The typographic interaction is unrelated to the player’s main job.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean, familiar sports-facility dashboard, executed with care.
canonCard.viewport: A named RallyLoop shell with ordinary session navigation, court status, a queue table, and clear actions.
canonCard.risk: The expected category pattern offers little distinctive sports identity.
